reason: E2 and E3 directly support the observation of edge-dislocation dominance and its link to high-temperature strength in specific refractory HEAs, but the proposed mechanism of 'thermal super-jogging' and the role of homogeneous lattice distortions are not evidenced in the cited passages, leaving key mechanistic premises unsupported.
premises: In BCC refractory HEAs, edge dislocations can dominate plasticity at elevated temperatures, contrary to conventional BCC alloys.
This edge-dislocation dominance is linked to a yield strength plateau and reduced thermal softening.
Thermal super-jogging on edge dislocations is the mechanism that stabilizes yield strength.
Homogeneous lattice distortions in the BCC phase favor edge over screw dislocation nucleation and activation.
The predicted behavior is specific to homogenized, single-phase refractory HEAs in the 600–1073 K range.
